knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=In lolliplot and dandelion.plot, controls the plot style (e.g., "pin", "fan", "pie", "circle", "flag", "pie.stack") ;; rescale=In lolliplot, a logical, numeric vector, data.frame, or character ("exon", "exon_99", "intron") to rescale the x-axis to emphasize specific regions ;; maxgaps=In dandelion.plot, controls dandelion density (numeric fraction or GRanges object) ;; operator=In viewTracks, a character vector (e.g., "+", "-") to combine/subtract tracks ;; theme=In optimizeStyle, sets the theme style ("bw", "col", "safe") ;; yaxis/xaxis=Controls axis drawing and custom label positions
- alternatives: Gviz and rtracklayer are mentioned. trackViewer is preferred over Gviz for lower memory/CPU consumption (especially with large WIG files, as it imports the entire file first and parses it later during plotting) and for specialized plots like lollipop/dandelion plots.
- when_to_use: Appropriate when visualizing NGS coverage data (ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, etc.) alongside gene annotations, or when plotting dense mutation, SNP, or methylation data (lollipop/dandelion plots), or chromatin interaction data (Hi-C).
- pitfalls: WIG files do not contain strand info, so strand must be set manually after import ;; For pie plots in lolliplot, score must be removed because pie considers all numeric columns except specific metadata columns (color, fill, alpha, shape, lwd, id, id.col), and at least 2 value columns are required ;; Total height for all tracks in viewTracks must sum to 1 when adjusting track heights ;; For pie.stack layout, metadata must contain stack.factor (and cannot be stack.factor.order or stack.factor.first) ;; lolliplot does not support parameters to set the title and xlab directly; users must use grid.text to add them.

workflows.name: genomic_track_visualization
workflows.intent: Import NGS coverage data (WIG/BED), build gene models, and visualize them as aligned track layers.
workflows.stages: 1. Import score data using importScore ;; 2. Set strand information manually ;; 3. Calculate coverage using coverageGR ;; 4. Build gene models using geneModelFromTxdb ;; 5. Optimize track styles using optimizeStyle ;; 6. Plot tracks using viewTracks
workflows.code:
repA <- importScore(file.path(extdata, "cpsf160.repA_-.wig"), file.path(extdata, "cpsf160.repA_+.wig"), format="WIG")
strand(repA$dat) <- "-"
strand(repA$dat2) <- "+"
fox2 <- importScore(file.path(extdata, "fox2.bed"), format="BED", ranges=GRanges("chr11", IRanges(122830799, 123116707)))
dat <- coverageGR(fox2$dat)
fox2$dat <- dat[strand(dat)=="+"]
fox2$dat2 <- dat[strand(dat)=="-"]
trs <- geneModelFromTxdb(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, org.Hs.eg.db, gr=gr)
optSty <- optimizeStyle(trackList(repA, fox2, trs))
trackList <- optSty$tracks
viewerStyle <- optSty$style
viewTracks(trackList, gr=gr, viewerStyle=viewerStyle)

workflows.name: lollipop_plot
workflows.intent: Visualize genomic variants, mutations, or methylation sites as lollipop markers over gene/protein features.
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare variant GRanges with metadata (score, color, shape) ;; 2. Prepare feature GRanges with metadata (fill, height) ;; 3. Plot using lolliplot
workflows.code:
SNP <- c(10, 12, 1400, 1402)
sample.gr <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(SNP, width=1, names=paste0("snp", SNP)))
features <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 501, 1001), width=c(120, 400, 405), names=paste0("block", 1:3)))
lolliplot(sample.gr, features)

workflows.name: dandelion_plot
workflows.intent: Visualize high-density methylation or mutation data where standard lollipop plots would overlap excessively.
workflows.stages: 1. Import methylation data ;; 2. Build gene model features ;; 3. Plot using dandelion.plot with specified type ("pin", "fan", "pie", "circle")
workflows.code:
methy <- import(system.file("extdata", "methy.bed", package="trackViewer"), "BED")
gr <- GRanges("chr22", IRanges(50968014, 50970514, names="TYMP"))
trs <- geneModelFromTxdb(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, org.Hs.eg.db, gr=gr)
features <- c(range(trs[[1]]$dat), range(trs[[5]]$dat))
names(features) <- c(trs[[1]]$name, trs[[5]]$name)
features$fill <- c("lightblue", "mistyrose")
features$height <- c(.02, .04)
dandelion.plot(methy, features, ranges=gr, type="pin")

workflows.name: chromatin_interaction_visualization
workflows.intent: Plot genomic interaction data (Hi-C/GInteractions) as a heatmap track alongside coverage tracks.
workflows.stages: 1. Convert GInteractions to track using gi2track ;; 2. Set track style parameters (breaks, color) ;; 3. Plot using viewTracks
workflows.code:
gi <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "nij.chr6.51120000.53200000.gi.rds", package="trackViewer"))
range <- GRanges("chr6", IRanges(51120000, 53200000))
tr <- gi2track(gi)
ctcf <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ctcf.sample.rds", package="trackViewer"))
setTrackStyleParam(tr, "breaks", c(seq(from=0, to=50, by=10), 200))
setTrackStyleParam(tr, "color", c("lightblue", "yellow", "red"))
viewTracks(trackList(ctcf, tr, heightDist=c(1, 3)), gr=range, autoOptimizeStyle = TRUE)
